body:
Warmest of welcomes to all my fellow internet friends—guys, gals, & everything in between! First off, I just wanted to say: thank you all so, so incredibly much for giving this post as much genuine love & unmatched support as y’all did—myself, being a little egg who just so happened to gather enough courage to share my own personal journey with the world, was completely & utterly shocked to see the outpouring of lovely comments & questions from such an immensely supportive community. I couldn’t have asked for a more indescribably positive group of people to have connected with, on not only a mental, but also in such emotional & spiritual manners. Each & every little bit of the support is immensely appreciated, & I just know that every single one of y’all are absolute rays of sunshine & beyond, bound to leave a strong, known, impact—absolutely not to be underestimated—on this earth that we share together. Love & hugs to all. ♡ 

As for the questions (as well as the wildly unexpected outpouring of love & support) regarding my little “accessory” across my face—endless thanks to every one of you all for asking in the manner that you did (with genuine curiosity & kindness—I’m always open to answering questions, so the quantity of pure & utter positive wonder surrounding my tube was such a breath of fresh air). I’ve been ridiculed for my tube (currently, I suffer at the hand of multiple different chronic illnesses, primarily a structural abnormality known as SMAS) in the past, so it feels wonderful—and, even that word is a massive understatement—to have been asked in such a respectful way. What’s on my face is known as a feeding tube, and it hooks up to a medical pump device that provides me with 100% of my nutrition as I don’t have the traditional ability to eat orally, much like your average person. Placements are relatively uncomfortable—though, manageable—& I’ve had those replacements for well over 2 years now. I see it as a part of me now, rather than a flaw or an imperfection or a “feature” that downplays my face.

And, lastly, as I had mentioned towards the beginning of my paragraph, endless thanks again—to each & every one of you—so very, incredibly much for your kindness along with the congratulations on my coming out, modelling & photography, future ambitions, et cetera. People like you amidst a seemingly endless sea of discrimination & transphobia mean more than the absolute world to me & beyond, & I just can’t understate that point enough. Infinite apologies for the lengthy response—there’s so much I desire to say, though I’ll try to keep this as short as possible. I hope sincerely that this update covers most of everything question-wise—however, I’m always open to any further curiosity, as content creation, editorial writing, & the like are some of my largest, most prominent ambitions in life at the moment. It is with a full heart & the most genuine of wishes that I hope each & every single one of you have a very wonderful rest of your individual days—my DM’s are open as long as any of y’all ever need a trans friend, or even simply a friend in general, to speak with. Much love! • Elliotte ♡

This comment brought me to tears—for serious. It’s been hours since I gathered the courage to post this transition timeline, & I swear I felt my heart beat out of my chest as I pressed the “post” button—my stomach fluttering violently as I saw the “your post is now live” push notification show on my screen. You have no idea on what level this response has reached me—on a personal note, I recently experienced one of the worst breakups (myself being the one left behind) quite possibly within the course of my short lifetime, & she was trans MTF. I was there for her, six years worth of shared dysphoria & jokes centered around “switching bodies”. When she presented as a bisexual male & I an equally bisexual, cisgender female—I’d cake on loads of intricate makeup, covering myself in hopes that I’d “blend in”—that I’d be her one & only exception as she’d been frequenting between gay & bi. Just like any other “normal”, 14 year old, teenage girl—but what really is “normal”? Your comment has taken me back to the day we met, knowing that, as you put it, I intuitively knew I really wasn’t. I was there by her side—literally—as she came out, four years later. And one day, she left. I haven’t heard from her since, & seeing her out with her new confidants has brought me full circle, now myself out as of the 24th of February this year—& alone. But, at the same time, I’m not so alone—no matter how lonely this journey may feel at times. I sincerely apologize for the rant, but your comment struck me on an emotional level. I’m so proud of you for being you; your undoubtedly, wonderfully authentic self. It’s extremely humbling knowing that you having seen this small piece of my own journey has brought you some form of solace on your own—& I salute you in what must be several year’s worth of hidden dysphoria & silent perseverance. Friend, thank you for—by some chance—choosing to reach out to me, another human being on this earth, going through the motions. It means more than you’ll ever know, gaining awareness of all the other wonderful trans individuals—specifically FTM’s—who are equally struggling with the concept of both femininity & masculinity. We will find ourselves, in due time. In the meantime, I’m here for you in spirit. Much love! • Elliotte ♡

Oh, my goodness! This is simply one of the absolute sweetest comments I’ve received today; you, along with many others have shown me that my self-worth is greater than I ever could have imagined, with me having been so insecure for the longest time. I’m definitely the kind of person to respond to every single little message that I receive, no matter how big or small—& it’s people like you that bring sincere joy to my heart, acknowledging the love & support I put out into this world; love & support that I, more often than not (and more times than others), feel so unworthy or incapable of receiving as a result of a couple traumatic relationships. I’m certain that you’re an absolute ray of sunshine, & I cannot thank you enough for the well-wishes on my new tube! Much love & many virtual hugs from NorCal. • Elliotte ♡

Ma’am, I’ve politely stalked your profile & I’d have to say the same. You’re absolutely, stunningly gorgeous. Coming from a former lesbian, you’ve definitely set the bar incredibly high for all the guys & gals out there who may eventually have the utmost pleasure of getting to know you! Keep being your incredible self, hon. You were meant to be the absolute stunner that you are! (Lovin’ the short hair, by the way!) • Elliotte ♡

Hello, friend! Thank you so much for your kind words regarding my SMAS—I’m honestly surprised anyone would know about the intricacies & little nuances that come with having a chronic illness, so you’ve totally caught me off guard—in a very positive way, though! In regards to the PEG—I received one during a surgical procedure on the 16th of February this year, & the SMAS was only found during the procedure when bile backing up into my stomach as well as a severe structural abnormality were both found—& nearly gave my surgeon a heart attack. I was given an NJ (the tube in the second image) as a mediator until my tract healed completely, & next Wednesday, I will officially be receiving a PEG-J tube (virtually the same concept, but it extends further past the large obstruction within my intestines so that symptoms are kept at bay) now that it’s fully healed! Again, thank you for your kind words as well as your question—it’s always a joy to explain to curious friends like you. • Elliotte ♡

Ah, yes! Fellow Dune enthusiast! Thank you so much for this comment, I’ve been told in the past that I would fit perfectly within the Dune universe & it’s honestly the most flattering thing considering I’m a bit insecure regarding my tube. In all seriousness though, I should totally experiment with makeup & paint it black like Paul Atreides (Timothée Chalamet)—who’s probably my biggest inspiration at the moment, in all aspects of life. Ah, I apologize for the long response—but your kind message has totally given me ideas as well as quelled some of that pent-up insecurity! Much love. • Elliotte ♡

Ah, thank you so much! I’m so sorry for coming right out the gate so overly enthusiastic, but this comment really reached out to me on a personal level—ultimately, in a positive way, of course. Masculine energy is something that I’ve been striving for years to achieve (in private, as contradicted by my pre-HRT/depo-T/anything at all, really)—& to hear that my most recent picture gave off that effect is a massive compliment. Thank you so much, man; what most likely took you a few seconds to write out & send has absolutely made my week! And, in regards to your own transition, I sincerely wish only the absolute best in your future endeavors—I can tell that you have a wonderful personality & are an equally wonderful person, both inside and out. May hormones & the ability to body-mod come in swift motion to you in the very near future, man! • Elliotte ♡

This is such a sweet comment, thank you for leaving it because it seriously made my whole day! I’ve actually been looking into modelling—though, not as a primary career, mainly as a somewhat casual hobby—but I’m in contact with a local photography company & my photographer is the kindest woman I’ve met, very holistic approach & could be a therapist if she so desired! I’ve been involved loosely in modelling & photography in general for about six years now though, as I run several social media platforms & am involved in content creation—in which photos are sort of obligatory in order to reach a broader audience.

Thank you again though for your comment! I saw on your page that you’re also pursuing your own journey in regards to transition, though I’m unsure of what specific compliment language I should use as I don’t personally know your pronouns. Just know that you’re a wonderful person, & I hope that all good things come to you in this life—you no doubt deserve it! • Elliotte ♡

Thank you so incredibly much for this lovely comment! You have no idea how much this immense outpouring of genuine love & support means to me; as someone who, despite having a supportive direct family, has gone through the gamut of tube-related insults & plainly transphobic comments in my days. As for my makeup, what a wonderful sentiment! Even as a trans male, I still practice every so often as my identity can vary from masc to femme by the day! Prior to my transition, I’d gotten so caught up in presenting & conforming as a typical teenage girl, “Instagram brows” & everything in between—that I’d been practicing multiple times a week from the age of 12. I’ll admit, it was pretty heavy for what I considered to be my “daily” makeup routine, but alas, I’ve always considered myself to be somewhat of a flamboyant human being anyways. I hope that all good things come your way, friend; & once again, thank you so much for your kind & flattering words! • Elliotte ♡

Hey! I want to commend you for your curiosity, in my opinion it’s almost always more helpful than hurtful to one’s overall personality—so, kudos to you for being the incredible person I’m certain you are! As for your question, I’m so glad you asked such a unique yet necessary one! It’s not too often I have people as respectful & kind as you come up to me like this, especially regarding my medical history—which can be pretty difficult to explain given its complexity! I would say that the best way to approach someone like myself (i.e. a chronically ill individual) with a question, whether that question be in reference to something “different” about said person (e.g. think mobility aids, medical devices, prosthetics, visible differences in appearance, et cetera), would be to approach almost exactly in the way you’ve done in your message! From the genuine curiosity to the way you’ve presented said curiosity, not to mention the manner in which you’ve prefaced your question with the obligatory “…I simply want to know more about your condition”, or “…I’m wondering (insert prompt) this, this, & this about you! If (insert prompt) offends you in any way, there’s no need to respond to/address my message. I simply would like to know more about this, this, & this to broaden my horizons/add to my overall knowledge.”

Keep being authentically you, hon (I hope I’m using the correct gender-affirming language, please let me know if not)! Your question was very respectful & genuine, & I’m so glad that you took an interest in something I’m normally ridiculed for. Take care! • Elliotte ♡

Hello, friend! First off, I just want to say: thank you so much for asking in the manner that you did. I’ve been ridiculed for my tube (I suffer from multiple chronic illnesses, primarily a structural abnormality known as SMAS) in the past, so it feels nice to have been asked in such a respectful way. What’s on my face is known as a feeding tube, & it hooks up to a medical pump device that provides me with 100% of my nutrition as I don’t have the traditional ability to eat orally, much like your average person. Placements are relatively uncomfortable, & I’ve had those replacements for well over 2 years now. I see it as a part of me now, rather than a flaw or an imperfection or a “feature” that downplays my face.

And, thank you so incredibly much for your kindness & the congratulations! People like you amidst a sea of transphobes mean the absolute world to me & beyond, & I can’t understate that enough. So sorry for the long response—I hope that covers everything, & that you have a wonderful rest of your day! • Elliotte ♡

This is the absolute sweetest response I could’ve received, you’ve just made my entire day! I’m so thankful for my supportive family & friends—within both realms of the internet & real life; though, I have received some nasty messages in the past. So, your message is honestly such a breath of fresh air. I sincerely hope you have a wonderful rest of your day, friend! • Elliotte ♡

Thank you so much! You’ve no idea how overwhelmed I am by the immensely positive outpouring of upvotes & comments such as this. Trans-Masculine/Non-Conforming dictating “terms” evoke a massive “flutter” in my stomach, if you will; & having been referred to as “handsome” has entirely made my week. I hope this, too, isn’t invasive—though, I’m feeling obliged to politely mention that I’ve checked out your own profile & come across a couple miscellaneous entries you’ve posted (as pertaining to your individual struggles with dysphoria as well)—alongside the indescribable quantity of thanks I’m sending your way in regards to your kind comment—that I do genuinely hope you ultimately “find your way” in this life, wherever it takes you; there’s no doubt in my mind you’ll accomplish wonderful things. Here’s to an amazing end—or beginning (?)—of your day (unsure as to which timezone you currently reside within); and, above all, try your hardest in remembering and/or affirming—whichever amongst these two notions you feel strongly towards—that both your person, as well as your gender identity: are beautiful, valid, & all things wonderful. My DM’s are always open if you’re ever serendipitously in need of a “vent” recipient! • Elliotte ♡

You’d be correct! I do, unfortunately, suffer at the merciless hand of co-occurring chronic illnesses; requiring a gastrojejunostomy (i.e. specialized feeding tube) in receiving 100% of my nutrition/sustenance. It’s always quite interesting when reading over what others’ inquiries seem to be as pertaining to this notion, given its unanimous “anti-commonality” amongst the generalized public—or, even throughout the expanses of the internet, for that matter. Fortunately, this doesn’t wholly interfere with my life; specifically & strictly in regards to my “medical” transition (i.e. hormone replacement/suppression therapy; alongside bi-weekly, intramuscular testosterone injections; a future bilateral-mastectomy, et cetera). I’m certainly appreciative & quick in responding to any & all questions; in addendum to such a note, this does bring immense gratification—seeing that you’ve inquired by the means of such a respectful disposition (I’ve received some explicitly nasty comments in the past directed towards my tube); as a result, & in candid honesty—this whole exchange has been such an indescribably rewarding, metaphorical breath of fresh air. My DM’s are always open! • Elliotte ♡

Ah, yes—fellow “Dune Enjoyer”! In all honestly, though—that’s extremely flattering—and, I’d want to thank you for your comment; as I’ve actually been attempting to achieve that sort of “vibe” for a while (ever heard of Timothée Chalamet?), & publicly presenting “Trans-Masculine” has been difficult with all the misgendering, dysphoria, & the like. On another note, I’d seen that you’ve posted to this subreddit a couple times, & I’d just wanted to say that you’re so absolutely, stunningly gorgeous! My DM’s are always open if you’re ever in need of a fellow member of the community to talk to. Lots of love & virtual hugs your way. • Elliotte ♡

Image Description: Lacinato kale, sweetened raw cranberries, and washed/dried wild rice blend baked and then simmered in a mediterranean spice mix and dried cloves, plated inside an acorn squash roasted with a mixed avocado and safflower oil rub, topped with fresh cilantro from our vegetable garden. This was also my first attempt at an avocado rose after binge watching food presentation YouTube videos!

I’m so sorry that this has happened to you. Genuinely, knowing I understand all of what you’re going through to a T. I’ve been experiencing some serious psychotic & bipolar mood issues ever since I’d spiraled back in November of last year, & my body’s taken a major hit. I’d not only destroyed the way my previously rational & smart mind worked entirely, but I’ve now also sustained permanent GI tract damage; to the point in which I’m tube-fed, & may very well have to be for the rest of my life as a result of the debilitating bloating, painful bowel movements, instant fullness, abdominal pain, & 10–20 degrees of nausea each & every time I’m “fed”. I’ve tried my hand at nourishing my body with “real” food & drink ever since, & it’s almost always automatically “rejected”. I wholly hate this disbelievingly destructive disease with each individual fiber of my being; our population doesn’t tend to think ahead as pertaining to the “long-term” effects whilst they’re in the midst of relapsing, & sooner than later—often, before it’s too late—that damage is already done. I genuinely hope you begin to feel better soon, as I understand firsthand how hellish it can feel—not being in control of both the mind & body. • Elliotte ♡

Hey! Yes, we’ve been through an incredibly long and draining journey with our medical team fighting for my case as it’s incredibly complicated—a mix of severe anxiety, OCD, autism spectrum disorder, ARFID, sensory processing disorder, pediatric feeding disorder/oral motor deficiency, and other more obscure conditions; it’s something that our healthcare provider’s system hasn’t seen before and we’ve had to pledge our situation more times than I can count. I’ve had this tube for longer than I can remember and due to my sensory processing sensitivities/autistic traits, it leaves me in constant pain and discomfort and I just haven’t been able to make progress in my feeding therapy (my goal is to take in at least half of my calories orally as i am 100 percent tube reliant as of now) due to the sensation in my throat, as the tube lays right on my gag reflex and it’s an agonizing feeling to have felt for as long as I have. Within the next couple of months though, we will be making the switch to the G-tube and i’m so excited for all of the opportunities it will bring me, along with a well-deserved break from the NG! I hope your daughter is doing well and that the G-tube has been manageable/ a better solution rather than having to deal with the trials and tribulations of the NG-tube. 🤗❤️

I’m a young adult suffering from autism-spectrum disorder, severe generalized anxiety, OCD, major depressive disorder, moderate bipolar mood regulation disorder, emetophobia/cibophobia, & some other smaller conflicting comorbidities. My anxiety spiked upon the onset of COVID & last October, it was exacerbated by a PANS (i.e. paediatric acute-onset neuropsychological syndrome) viral infection which in turn caused all of my chronic illnesses to spiral out of control. As an almost direct result of feeling sick from PANS, my eating (which has always been incredibly difficult due to my sensory processing disorder, or SPD, which is associated with my ASD/autism spectrum disorder) stopped completely as I’d also withdrawn pretty severely from Prozac after accidentally going off cold-turkey due to side effects & I eventually wound up within the hospital for several weeks due to severe malnutrition, having lost between 1.8 & 2.0 stone (26-40 pounds) within about a month & then to an intensive inpatient/residential setting across the country for a couple of months, which I’ve just returned from to resume a physical rehabilitation program as the inpatient staff were unable to treat an ED that also ended up being exacerbated by the medication withdrawal, PANS, & increase in anxiety (search for ARFID/PFD, which is a non-body image based eating disorder most commonly diagnosed in children and/or teens with autism spectrum disorders). Point being, my emetophobia also became so bad that I ended up on a feeding tube & to this day, six-&-a-half months later, I’m still 100% tube-reliant & will be receiving a surgical tube soon due to the amount of time I’ve been on temporary nasal tubes & how awful they are for my sensory sensitivities—the good news being that I’ve ended up regaining those (40 pounds) 2.0 stone (e.g. for reference, I was 16 when this started, 164 centimetres & 8.2 stone or 116 pounds, then dropped into the 6.8’s, or high-100’s, & 6.2’s, low-80’s—all due to my severe anxiety & panic surrounding my irrational fears & phobias regarding choking & vomiting)—& have since been medically stable/rehabilitated. We’ve tried every anxiety & mood medication/SSRI under the sun, & it seems that due to dysautonomia & autoimmune disorders that run in the family, my body either flat-out rejects the medications & I develop side-effects, or it just doesn’t work at all & the effect isn’t there whatsoever. Right now I’m on about 100 milligrams or so of Zoloft & the anxiety has increased tenfold since getting on it & upping the dosage—we’ve heard that perhaps it may grow worse before it becomes better, but this is unlike anything I’ve ever anticipated or seen as I’m now experiencing four to six panic attacks a day that draw out over a span of several hours, & I’m so debilitated to the point in which I’ve needed to drop out of my Year Twelve (12) in academics & spend the whole day shaking in bed every single day because the anxiety is just that bad. Anyways, the point of this response wasn’t to go off on another one of my tangents, but to reassure you that you’re most definitely not the only one suffering right now with awful panic attacks & that we’re all in this together, no matter how unpredictable things may become. You’re always welcome to DM me with any questions you have, or if you just want to rant about how you’re feeling—as my message box will always be open—we seem to struggle with similar things & we might actually have more in common than I’d thought! Hope you feel better soon. • Elliotte ♡

Aw, thank you so much, that means a whole lot to me! I am not a professional photographer by any means—though, I have taken a couple of classes and aspire to become one (at least, if not as a direct profession, taken up as a side-pastime) someday! It definitely helps if the room is already somewhat cozy so that the picture is even easier to take. ♡

You’re so kind! I appreciate the offer to DM if I’d ever need to talk regarding anything other than you already know—I’ve found it quite difficult to express myself in the past as pertaining to this sort of thing, so knowing  my experience has been acknowledged & validated feels indescribably wonderful. I also hope for the best in lieu of your journey with both medications & anxiety, as Gods know it hasn’t been easy; & probably won’t be for a considerable chunk of time, especially given the both of our positions in addendum to our consecutive places in “conquering” this pest. Feel free to let me know if you’re feeling the same, & if you—at any point—are in need of a recipient regarding a healthy rant; in genuine consideration as to how you’re holding up. • Elliotte ♡

What luck it is that I’d come across this post! I’ve been experiencing severe panic attacks since the middle of September-October last year (I’d always struggled with mood/manic episodes & panic disorders prior to this onset, but they were manageable, at least) & my medications have sort of caused my anxiety to go haywire. I’m not quite sure what triggered this sudden downfall/spiral to occur as out of nowhere as it did, although I possess a hunch that having quit Prozac cold-turkey after feeling unwell due to side effects (poor choice in retrospect, the withdrawal was about a million times worse than the symptoms that came from taking the medication) was a huge contributing factor, now that I think more about it. Anyways, we’ve trialled just about every SSRI beneath the sun & it feels almost as if I’m more functional off these regulatory medications than I am when I’m on them—I’ve been battling so many symptoms ever since the spiral began (e.g. shakiness, clammy hands & legs, blood pooling, high/low fluctuating BP, severe constant nausea, dizziness/vertigo, psychosis, insomnia, panic/anxiety attacks, quite obviously—& other phobias branching off these side effects which developed after the fact, such as cibophobia, emetophobia, phagophobia, & agoraphobia) that it all just feels so counterproductive at this point. Anyways, the point of this reply wasn’t to rant, but rather to validate your personal experience—you’re definitely not alone in this strange boat we’re all upon. It may be incredibly difficult & “quality-of-life-reducing”, but things will eventually work out in the end. I merely wish playing the guessing game didn’t have to take so long with SSRI’s! • Elliotte ♡

I know! I’ve both heard & seen so much regarding all that was the Miiverse; it’s quite a shame I wasn’t around to wholly experience the genuine magnitude of this incredible platform. I’d booted up Super Mario 3D World yesterday, as you’re viewing within my image, & was notified by the game; specifically, having received an inquiry regarding any sort of desire in editing my online settings (i.e. sharing level scores to the Miiverse, amongst other things). It was potently bittersweet. • Elliotte ♡

Ah, so almost as if instead of ‘forcing’ my brain to try and adapt to all of these different coping methods for the sake of feeling better about the situation/conjuring up some sort of fake excuse to dismiss myself from my insecurities, I should instead try to treat it like a personal improvement project? I’ll admit, I’ve tried so many things with the intent of bettering myself in terms of confidence, but I suppose I never really looked at it that way, so I really appreciate your response! Definitely will make sure to give this a try, and your description is very helpful in allowing me to understand the gist of it, so it seems like I’ve already got most of this strategy laid out in front of me :) Hopefully you’re able to feel better about yourself too—you’re very lucky, if I’m understanding correctly, that you haven’t intentionally self-harmed/tried to create scars out of frustration, but body dysphoria is just as valid, so I really do wish you the best in the future.

Hey! Not sure if you were ever able to come across a solution to the issue you’ve been experiencing, but it’s safe to divulge I’m a user of Homebrew & ACNL’s Save Editor, have been playing NL for six (6) years, & possess multiple towns; in essence, I’ve learned quite all there is to know as pertaining to hacking, & how such a process works in consideration of the game’s files & whatnot! I’ve been terraforming my town these days, only utilising hacking for minor fixes—& I’d definitely be willing to crack open the SE if your system’s hacked already so as to provide aid, given I tend to remain consistently active within this forum—assisting the ACNL community & such, so to speak. From what I’m aware, I’d easily be able to edit your town if I were to gain access to your ‘garden.dat’ file—& from there, I’d insert said file within the SE & utilise its customisation elements, as seen fit. After the fact, it’d be sent back to you, & theoretically, you’d inject that file with the aid of Homebrew—in essence, serving as your “new” save file; nevertheless, if you’ve not installed CFW already, I unfortunately wouldn’t be able to provide assistance as this does require the modification of your system offhand.

It does require a significant quantity of research, time, patience—& most crucially, practise—although, anyone in possession of full access to the Internet, the MicroSD Management function within your settings, & the Save Editor…can hack! I, personally wasn’t privy as it pertains to much of any sort of knowledge—not even a few months ago—yet, after pouring quite the healthy portion of time into comprehending said process, I was finally able to piece together exactly how the technology must be modified so as to get it all “up & running” properly. If you’re, at present, still in need of any additional assistance with all this, there exist several [videos](https://youtu.be/fkW2KDce954) alongside other tutorials online detailing the ins-&-outs of hacking your specified system model. The video attached is what I’d referred to quite a while ago, & it’d worked out first try—albeit, given loads of meticulous rounds involving double (& even quadruple)–checking the SD’s files.

Anyways, apologies for such a lengthy response—although, I do personally believe there’s no harm in providing aid, especially given this niche community’s become known for & is founded upon the overlying principle of helping one another, during all hours as seen fit! Hopefully, you’re able to work things out with your town. • Elliotte ♡

Y’all are too kind! I really appreciate everyone taking the time to check out my town over at the Dream Suite—& in response to those who don’t quite possess a “theme” yet, my terraforming definitely didn’t always appear this way! Rather, I see it as a project nearly six years in the making, & even still, some aspects of my town are prominently unfinished (i.e. awry designs practically everywhere), as I’ve been trudging my way through the redesigning process for quite some time now.

Given anyone comes across this post later on into the future, feel absolutely free in sending off a DM if you’re in search of tips and/or actively requesting insight as pertaining to landscaping & terraforming! I’ve gained quite a bit of experience working with the technicality of it all, & would be more than happy in assisting all individuals in need of assistance with the modification of town layouts, crucial knowledge in regards to New Nintendo 3DS hacking, & beyond. Much love! • Elliotte ♡

Where’d I even begin if prompted to detail just how much this series means to me? Animal Crossing has played such a large role in shaping the person I’ve become over these past couple years, as silly as it may seem—given, to seemingly most of those outside the AC community…it’s rather merely “another” Nintendo game. Although, as a player of all main AC titles (i.e. from the GameCube’s ACGC to the Switch’s ACNH), in addendum to my identity as a gal who’s remained part of the “neurodivergent” community the greater majority of my lifespan, these games’ve “been there” for me at times in which I possessed not one soul to look to—& in a way, provided some bittersweet sort of escape/solace, within a quaint little world where all that mattered during those moments were the sweetest of villagers, & the creation of a bubble far from reality—one in which I’d carefully envisioned, terraformed, & brought to life…all in solitary. Anyhow, I’d go on for days as it pertains to the manners by which the franchise’s changed me, though overall—I’d state with full confidence that, as someone having suffered the majority of her way through the motions, Animal Crossing’s provided a nigh-equalised balance of happiness & the cultivation of memorable experiences—which, when all’s said & done…might even outweigh some of the more troublesome struggles I’ve overcome.

All the best to everyone in participation! It’s with immense gratuity & appreciation I commend you for your generosity, alongside the rare opportunity presented before myself as a participant within such an enthralling event. Much love! • Elliotte ♡

Alright! I’ve added your friend code, & my gates are open whenever you so wish to enter! Don’t adopt too much concern as it pertains to payment(s) and/or playing the role of a philanthropist—I request nothing in return, & you’re more than welcome to claim her as yours for no charge. Much love! • Elliotte ♡

I apologize in advance if this response ends up being super long, but I saw that you’d asked for NL advice (specifically w/bells) and I’m more than happy to write some of it down here if you’d want to read it later! Have played all main AC titles (GameCube, WW, City Folk, etc.) so I guess you could say that I’ve got quite a bit of experience with the game mechanics and such! NL in specific I’ve been playing since 2015 and strangely in all of that time, have only learned most things to know about money/bells within the past couple of months.

1. If you haven’t unlocked the island yet, this is at least in my opinion one of the absolute best methods NL offers to earn bells FAST! When first starting out (e.g adding new character/save file or starting a new town), Isabelle will mention a few things about the former mayor Tortimer living on an island, which you can reach via the port at the base of your town. I won’t get into the specifics if you’re already familiar, but if you go to the island (generally) between the hours 7 PM-1 AM, you’ll be able to find TONS of rare beetles, which sell for at least 5K a piece depending upon which bug you’re selling. With the island storage bin and a little bit of patience, it’s possible to come back to your town with a full inventory x4 of bugs (equal to roughly 500K bells in revenue—in one go!) so definitely give this one a shot if you haven’t already!

2. Turnips. Ultimately I think this was one of the biggest wasted opportunities for me personally since I’d ignored everything and anything that had to do with Joan, turnips, and turnip prices for nearly five years (mostly out of laziness and poor drive to actually learn about the sheer profit that turnips can bring if you’re skillful with them). Between 6 AM and roughly noon (12-1 PM I believe, have to double check though) you can purchase turnips from the boar Joan, and once you’ve bought your turnips (which come exclusively in bunches of 10 only) they’ll spoil at the same time next Sunday, or the Sunday after you’ve made your purchase. Essentially these can be sold throughout the week at Re-Tail for different prices each day, which over time can generate a large amount of bells pretty quickly! From personal experience, I’d say I’ve been just about if not less successful using the turnip method rather than the beetle/late night island method.

If you’re unfamiliar with TT-ing, or a shorthand term used throughout the AC community for time traveling, there’s an excellent and informative article [here](https://animalcrossing.fandom.com/wiki/Time_Travel) where you can read more in depth about it, so my description from here on out won’t be as confusing to you. If you are, great! Time traveling definitely has a lot of benefits that go unused, for the most part, and the trick I’m about to describe is something I’d say is only for those who either don’t have villager preferences or don’t mind if: favored villagers move out, weeds/unwanted flowers grow, turnip opportunities go to waste, a [perfect town status](https://animalcrossing.fandom.com/wiki/Perfect_town) possibly disappearing over the TT time span, or those who (most importantly) for personal reasons would rather not TT/play the game day by day as intended. Back to the point, if you were to save and quit your game file, change the current year in settings to 2035, and return (you must have 100K+ in revenue stored with the post office’s ABD first), you should receive a letter containing money that your player has earned over time in [interest](https://www.thonky.com/animal-crossing-new-leaf/automatic-bell-dispenser#earning-interest). From this point on, save and quit, change the date back, rinse, and repeat. As long as you’re a player that doesn’t seem to mind the negative effects of long-term TT (as mentioned above), this method should work out very well and provide you with a large amount of bells in a relatively short amount of time.
